source_text:
Τοὺς δὲ ἀπεσταλμένους ἀφ̓ ἡμῶν Κλαύδιον Ἔφηβον καὶ Οὐαλέριον Βίτωνα σὺν καὶ Φορτουνάτῳ ἐν εἰρήνῃ μετὰ χαρᾶς ἐν τάχει ἀναπέμψατε πρὸς ἡμᾶς, ὅπως θᾶττον τὴν εὐκταίαν καὶ ἐπιποθήτην ἡμῖν εἰρήνην καὶ ὁμόνοιαν ἀπαγγέλλωσιν, εἰς τὸ τάχιον καὶ ἡμᾶς χαρῆναι περὶ τῆς εὐσταθείας ὑμῶν.
Ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μεθ̓ ὑμῶν καὶ μετὰ πάντων πανταχῆ τῶν κεκλημένων ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ δἰ αὐτοῦ. δἰ οὗ αὐτῷ δόξα, τιμή, κράτος καὶ μεγαλωσύνη, θρόνος αἰώνιος, ἀπὸ τῶν αἰώνων εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν. Ἐπιστολὴ τῶν Ῥωμαίων πρὸς τοὺς Κορινθίους.
thought_title: Send back the messengers in peace and joy
orientation: The Roman church is closing its letter to the Corinthians, asking them to send back the three messengers quickly so that the Romans may hear good news of restored harmony.
pass_a_gloss: But the ones sent from us, Claudius Ephebus and Valerius Biton, together with Fortunatus, send back to us in peace with joy quickly, so that they may report more swiftly the peace and harmony that we have prayed for and longed for, so that we too may rejoice more quickly about your stability. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you and with all everywhere who have been called by God through him. Through whom to him be glory, honor, might and majesty, an eternal throne, from the ages to the ages of the ages. Amen. Letter of the Romans to the Corinthians.

choices.why: Keeps the two prepositional phrases distinct and literal, matching the source's double qualifier for how the messengers are to be sent back.
Literal rendering of the adverbial phrase; the author repeats the idea with θᾶττον and τάχιον, so keeping 'quickly' preserves the urgency.
Both adjectives are passive verbal adjectives; rendering them as participles keeps the sense that the Romans have been praying for and longing for this peace and harmony.
The noun denotes a settled, stable condition; 'stability' is the most literal and neutral rendering.
Keeps the noun phrase as a separate item in the doxology list, matching the source's asyndetic series.

choices.term: Ἐπιστολὴ τῶν Ῥωμαίων πρὸς τοὺς Κορινθίους
choices.english: Letter of the Romans to the Corinthians
choices.why: This is a subscription title, not part of the letter body; rendered literally as a title.
rejected: The Epistle of the Romans to the Corinthians

pass_b_english: Send back to us quickly, in peace and with joy, the messengers we sent to you: Claudius Ephebus, Valerius Biton, and Fortunatus with them. Then they can report to us all the sooner the peace and harmony we have prayed for and longed for, and we too can rejoice all the sooner over your stability.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you and with all everywhere who have been called by God through him. Through him be glory, honor, might, and majesty to God, an eternal throne, from age to age, for ever and ever. Amen.
Letter of the Romans to the Corinthians.

polish.changed: Broke the long first sentence into two for easier reading, replaced the em dash with a colon, and clarified that 'they' refers to the messengers and 'we' to the Roman church.

last_rejected.why: εὐσταθείας means 'good standing' or 'steadfastness', not 'stability' in modern sense; better 'your good standing' or 'your steadfastness'.
last_rejected.ruling: εὐσταθείας means stability/steadfastness; 'stability' is within normal range, not a mistranslation.
